clue.text: Items dished up for hungry commando trainees?

definitions.text: Items dished up for hungry commando trainees?

parts.words: Items dished up for hungry commando trainees?
parts.note: reads as a menu of meals served to famished soldiers, but the courses meant are obstacle runs used in military training

explanation.surface: A canteen menu planned for ravenous recruits in commando training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courses' are the parts of a meal dished up, and also the training circuits commandos run; 'hungry' pushes the food reading.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle circuit for training soldiers is named this, and the second word also means stages of a meal.

clue.text: Worker I find under a tree in Ghana

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed under another follows it in the answer

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone discovers an employee sheltering beneath a tree in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' puts ANT and I below ASH. The definition is a loose pointer to a region and people of Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: This region of central Ghana, home of a historic kingdom and its people, lies within that country.

clue.text: Unused to tale-telling, oddly enough

parts.note: being strange to something means being unused to it, unfamiliar with it
to relate is to tell a story

explanation.surface: Someone unaccustomed to gossiping, surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unused to' looks like a single idea but splits in two, its 'to' kept as written; the three wordplay words also form the idiom itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic aside meaning surprisingly or curiously, used when reporting something unexpected.

clue.text: Isn't down as a poisonous growth

parts.note: something that is not down is up

explanation.surface: Something that is not low is described as a toxic plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The upas is a tropical tree whose sap was used as arrow poison.
explanation.definitionFit: The upas is a Javanese tree with toxic latex, legendary for poisoning anything near it.

clue.text: All the best from here? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of the phrase, so the answer sits inside it short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A postcard signing off with good wishes from the sender's location, cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' points to the phrase 'the best' minus its last letter. 'All the best from here?' reads as a holiday postcard sent from the ancient Egyptian city, which 'here' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The postcard's sender is writing from the ancient Egyptian city on the Nile, so 'here' is that place.

clue.text: Type who could be a poor relation

indicators.note: a poor version of the word is a badly made one, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a person who might be a needy family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor relation' looks like a single idiom but 'poor' is the anagram signal on RELATION; the dated sense 'type' is a kind of person from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Used here as a noun, a person from the Far East is a type of person, the clue's 'who' marking a human.

clue.text: Redress for the agent given an allowance

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative, an agent
the indefinite article gives the letter A
a ration is an allowed amount

explanation.surface: Compensation paid to a representative who receives a stipend.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean making amends or compensation for a wrong done.

clue.text: Men without exception

parts.note: describes all males, each being the child of a mother, as an idiom for everybody

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means every single man, since each one was born to a woman.

clue.text: Did the round trip awheel? .

parts.note: suggests going out and back by bicycle, while also hinting at going round in a repeating loop

explanation.definitionFit: Riding a bike, which runs on wheels, and passing through a repeating loop both describe this verb.

clue.text: Plants a piece of luggage in here

indicators.note: the luggage word is placed inside the word here

parts.note: a bag is a piece of luggage

explanation.surface: Someone stows a suitcase among the greenery in this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plants' looks like a verb (puts in place) but is the definition noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and leafy vegetation collectively, especially as pasture.

clue.text: Lack of respect from Bantu warriors yet to be mustered

parts.note: an impi is a Zulu regiment of warriors

indicators.note: mustering gathers troops into new order, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disrespect shown by African warriors who have not yet assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: An impi is a Zulu regiment; 'to be mustered' is the anagram signal on 'yet', as troops are gathered into new ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Impiety is irreverence, a want of respect especially towards God or duty.

clue.text: Zola heroine making an entrance in the U S or thereabouts

indicators.note: the word that follows is the piece being made to go in
entering something means going inside it

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North America, the US and its neighbourhood
taken as written

explanation.surface: A French novelist's heroine arriving in America or nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making ... entrance in' signals a container. Émile Zola's novel of that title follows a Parisian courtesan.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola wrote a novel named after its title character, a courtesan of the Second Empire.

clue.text: Minted piece of princely heritage?

parts.note: reads as a coin struck for a royal line, but describes a mint plant whose name splits into a coin and a regal word

explanation.definitionFit: Pennyroyal is a mint species, and its name joins a small coin to a word for kingly.

clue.text: Relative to one afloat, apparently

parts.note: describes a family member of a vessel, the term for one built to the same design as another

explanation.surface: Something that seems to be kin to a floating object.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel built to the same design as another is called its sibling in nautical usage.

clue.text: Two countries seen as one to Stalin's secret police chief

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
Lavrentiy Beria ran the Soviet secret police under Stalin

explanation.surface: To the Soviet security boss two nations looked like a single one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One to Beria' puts I before his name; the result names the peninsula that Spain and Portugal share.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula holding Spain and Portugal is named after the ancient Iberians, so it stands for those two countries.

clue.text: Rush for an old coin in Kent

parts.note: to dart is to rush
D was the abbreviation for the old British penny

explanation.surface: Someone hurries to buy an antique coin while in a county of England.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for the penny in Britain's pre-decimal currency. Dartford is a town in Kent, the county south-east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartford is a town on the Thames estuary located in the county of Kent.

clue.text: It's hard on a caretaker to rook a place where Gladstone lived and died

definitions.text: a place where Gladstone lived and died

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the next, coming before it

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a warden looks after a building or place
in chess the rook is also called the castle

explanation.surface: A caretaker finds it tough to cheat a landmark linked to a Victorian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To rook' looks like a verb meaning to swindle, but it is the chess piece. William Gladstone, a Victorian prime minister, lived at this house in north Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone, Britain's four-times prime minister, made his home at this house in Flintshire and died there in 1898.

clue.text: European changing at Cairo before noon

indicators.note: one piece comes ahead of the next in the answer
letters that are changing are moved into another order

explanation.surface: A traveller switching planes in Egypt's capital before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' is the anagram signal on 'at Cairo', which gives the country's name; 'before' puts it ahead of the noon letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Croatian is a native of Croatia, a country of south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: See 16
Trouble for two returning

parts.note: both means the two together

indicators.note: returning means the short word is read backwards

parts.note: re means concerning, about, in the sense of for

explanation.surface: Difficulty for a pair coming back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' stands for 're' in the sense of 'concerning', and 'returning' turns it round to follow the word for two.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a nuisance or difficulty that causes worry.

clue.text: It opens up a course you are seeking

definitions.text: It opens up a course you are seeking

parts.words: It opens up a course you are seeking
parts.note: describes something unfolded to show the route you are looking for, as a folded chart is opened

explanation.surface: Something that reveals the path a person is trying to find.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist's chart of streets and highways is unfolded to find a route, and the phrase also means a plan.

clue.text: Island the French cry about

parts.note: les is the French plural for the

indicators.note: turned about means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: An island where the French weep over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns the cry round after the French article. The island is a large one in the Aegean, off Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesbos is a large Greek island in the north-eastern Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Ocean flier when there's a war about

indicators.note: letters that are about are moved round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A seabird is spotted while fighting is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges the ten letters of THERE'S A WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearwaters are long-winged seabirds that skim the ocean waves.

clue.text: Region found in a particular Eastern republic

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of the next two words

explanation.surface: A district located in a certain country to the east.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district of land.

clue.text: … and another in the same area hard hit

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is another Greek island in the same part of the Aegean as the previous island clue
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Following on, a second island nearby takes a heavy blow.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue's island: COS, also spelt Kos, lies in the same sea. A cosh is a short heavy club.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosh someone is to strike them with a heavy bludgeon.

clue.text: Was unable to bear the cargo lying around

indicators.note: the cargo word lies around the other piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a load is a cargo

explanation.surface: Someone hated having freight left everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying around' makes the cargo word a container holding 'the'; 'Was unable to bear' is the definition, not a ship's capacity.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathed means hated, detested, could not stand something.

clue.text: Thrive as a liner in its heyday

definitions.text: Thrive as a liner in its heyday

parts.words: Thrive as a liner in its heyday
parts.note: suggests an ocean ship at its peak, but describes flourishing as a plant does in flower

explanation.surface: A passenger ship prospering in its best years.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to flourish or thrive, like a tree in flower at its best.

clue.text: How to meet adversity without looking down

definitions.text: How to meet adversity without looking down

parts.words: How to meet adversity without looking down
parts.note: describes staying cheerful in hard times, with looking down read both as being glum and as lowering the head

explanation.surface: Advice on facing hardship without dropping your gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stay cheerful and brave in trouble, literally holding the head high.
